summary.text: 同 is used for “same” or “alike,” and for “together with.” Early inscriptions use it for meeting or joining and for “along with”; scholars disagree over whether its earliest enclosing shape pictures an object or already represents 同.

formation.text: Early forms have an enclosure, sometimes with 口. One analysis tentatively interprets the enclosure as a picture of a tube- or bucket-like object; another reads the enclosure itself as 同 and treats 口 as optional. The object’s identity and name remain unconfirmed. A later received seal-script analysis parses the form as 𠔼, an enclosing or covering element, with 口, an inner mouth or opening. This later analysis does not settle the early disagreement.

components.text: One analysis tentatively interprets the early enclosure as a tube- or bucket-like picture; another reads it directly as 同. The object and its name are unconfirmed, so the proposed pictorial role is disputed.
In the received seal-script analysis, 𠔼 is the enclosing or covering element, including the upper horizontal stroke. This later parsing does not establish the enclosure’s role in the early graph.
In the received seal-script analysis, 口 is the inner mouth or opening within 𠔼. This later parsing does not establish whether it was part of the earliest form or its role there.

history.text: Early oracle-bone forms show an enclosure, sometimes with 口. Early Western Zhou bronze forms include the enclosure alone, while bronze forms more commonly include 口. The reported seal-script analysis parses the graph as 𠔼 plus 口, followed by clerical and regular forms. The curated seal-style image is a modern redraw, not a dated artifact.
In reported early forms, 同’s side strokes are symmetrical, unlike 凡, whose right stroke sweeps outward. This graphic distinction does not resolve the competing interpretations of 同’s enclosure.

uncertainties.text: The early enclosure may depict an object, but its identity, name, and pronunciation are not established. Borrowing the graph to write a tube- or bucket-related word therefore remains unconfirmed.
The cited examples document several uses but do not establish their precise dates or the semantic pathways connecting them.

senses.period: Oracle-bone inscriptions; exact dates not supplied
senses.text: Cited oracle-bone examples are interpreted as meeting or joining. This is the earliest use documented here, not necessarily the original meaning.

senses.text: An oracle-bone example is interpreted as “along with.” The evidence does not establish whether this use predates the meeting sense.

senses.period: Bronze inscriptions and later examples; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples include a use interpreted as making things alike; later examples attest “same” or “alike.” Their relationship to the earlier uses is unresolved.
Later examples attest a transitive use meaning to make things the same or unify them. Its development from another sense is not established.
Later examples attest uses glossed as following or assenting. Their connection to the other senses is unresolved.
Current definitions include “same,” “similar,” and “together with”; these glosses do not establish a chronology among the senses.

evidence.text: Sharing a common 凡 tongue 口
Pictograph of a bucket or tube, now written as 筒. 口 (mouth) indicates that the character is only "mouthed", i.e. only used for its phonetic value.
合會也。从𠔼从口。

Pictogram (象形): a pipe — original form of 筒 (OC *doːŋ, *doːŋs, “pipe”). 口 was added later to mark the opening and prevent confusion.
In early forms, 同 (tóng) and 凡 were distinguished not by the presence of 口, but by symmetry: 同 (tóng) is symmetrical, while 凡 (fán) has its right stroke sweeping outward.
Perhaps related to Tibetan སྡོང་བ (sdong ba, “to unite; to join”), Mizo intawng (inᴸ-tɔŋᴴ, “to meet together; to tally; to agree”), Mizo intawn (inᴸ-tɔn^F, “to meet together; to tally; to agree”). Unrelated to 叢 (OC *zloːŋ, “to collect; thicket”) (Schuessler, 2007).
合會也。从𠔼从口。

evidence.field: 甲骨字形、分歧分析、早期用例、語義
evidence.text: 該庫稱甲骨文同作從◎從口；裘錫圭認為◎可讀作同，可能是筒、桶一類器物的象形；王子揚則直接釋◎為同，並認為口可加可不加。庫中另記同的兩側豎筆對稱，凡不對稱，並列出西周早期天亡簋等金文材料。甲骨文例《合集》11171正+11176「乎同多沚」解作會同沚族長；《合集》32730用作連同。金文也有會同用法。這是字庫所報導的學者分析與釋例，器物說仍屬推測。
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

evidence.field: 同：許慎釋義及段玉裁注
evidence.text: 《說文》條目釋同為「合會也」，分析為「从𠔼从口」。段玉裁注以覆蓋下有口解說其意。這是漢代字書的歷史分析，不足以單獨裁定甲骨文較早字形的構形。
evidence.title: 說文解字「同」

evidence.text: 該庫引甲骨文作會同、連同，西周金文作會同及齊同；另列「相同、一樣」「使相同、統一」「共同、一起」「跟隨、附和」等後續用法，並舉《左傳》《清華簡》《睡虎地秦簡》等傳世文本或出土文獻例。所列材料支持這些用法存在，但單靠此條目不能建立各語義轉變的精確先後或因果鏈。
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

evidence.text: 《說文》釋衕為「通街也」，分析作「从行同聲」；段玉裁所見注本則作「从行，周聲」，並記「徒弄切」。這明確支持傳統字書將行作義符、同（或注本所稱周）作聲符；二者異文宜保留。
evidence.title: 說文解字「衕」

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文、簡帛與語義用例
evidence.text: The entry reports competing analyses of the oracle-bone enclosure shape: Qiu Xigui reads it as 同 and tentatively as a pictograph of a tube or bucket; Wang Ziyang reads it directly as 同, with 口 optional. It distinguishes 同 from 凡 by bilateral symmetry, reports an enclosure-only form on early Western Zhou bronzes and enclosure-plus-口 as common in bronze inscriptions, and says small-seal script was reinterpreted as 𠔼 plus 口, followed by clerical and regular forms. The entry cites oracle-bone uses for meeting/along-with (《合集》11171正+11176; 32730), early Western Zhou bronze uses for meeting and making alike, and later cited examples for same, unify, together, and follow/assent. Those examples establish uses, not a precise semantic chronology or pathway.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

evidence.field: 衕：說文、廣韻及讀音條目
evidence.text: The entry gives 說文’s 通街也、从行，同聲 and 徒弄切, and cites 廣韻 readings 徒紅 (平聲) and 徒弄 (去聲). It presents 行 as semantic component and 同 as sound component in the received dictionary analysis; no early dated use of 衕 is established by this entry.

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨文、金文字形及用例
evidence.text: The entry reports competing interpretations of the oracle-bone enclosure: Qiu Xigui tentatively reads it as a tube- or bucket-like pictograph, while Wang Ziyang reads it directly as 同 and treats 口 as optional. It distinguishes the symmetrical side strokes of 同 from 凡, reports enclosure-only early Western Zhou bronze forms and more common enclosure-plus-口 bronze forms, then says seal script was reinterpreted as 𠔼 plus 口 and continued into clerical and regular forms. The entry cites oracle-bone examples for meeting/along-with, bronze examples for meeting and making alike, and later examples for same, unify, together, and assent/follow. Its examples establish usages but not exact semantic chronology or the links between senses.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The pipe/tube/bucket interpretation of the early ◎ form is attributed to particular scholars by CUHK, while another scholar reads the shape directly as 同; the original object and its name/pronunciation are not independently established here. The claim that 同 was borrowed specifically for a homophonous object-name therefore remains unverified; a reconstruction of 同 alone would not prove the object's name.

No glyph image was visually inspected. The graphic sequence is reported from CUHK's prose: early oracle-bone ◎ with optional 口; bronze forms commonly ◎ plus 口; small-seal form reanalyzed as 𠔼 plus 口; clerical/regular form follows the seal form. Potential seal-stage reinterpretation is reported as the source's account, not direct image analysis.

The attested early senses collected here concern 同 as meeting/along-with and later sameness, unification, togetherness, and agreement. Exact dating and semantic pathways among them are not fully established by the inspected source.

No source in this pass established an early 衕 attestation date or whether 衕's use arose as a phonetic compound independently of its Shuowen-era gloss. The received Shuowen text and its variant注 analysis (同聲 versus 周聲) are recorded, not resolved.

Official Unicode Unihan character pages for 同 and 衕 could not be accessed by the web tool. Current readings tóng and tòng are only in the supplied local Unihan rows; official click-through verification is missing. The local Baxter–Sagart table provides 同 *lˤoŋ only, with no inspected external row for 衕, so no same-system sound comparison is asserted.
No reuse/license review was performed; no local extract is recommended from the sources inspected.

The enclosure-shape analysis remains disputed: CUHK attributes a tentative tube/bucket pictograph analysis to Qiu Xigui and a direct reading as 同 to Wang Ziyang. Neither establishes the original object's independently recoverable name or pronunciation, so a specific whole-graph phonetic-loan account for 筒/筒-like object remains unproven.
CUHK reports a seal-stage reinterpretation from the earlier enclosure shape to 𠔼 plus 口; this is the source's paleographic account, not direct inspection of artifacts in this research stage.

The cited early oracle-bone uses are glossed meeting/along-with; bronze examples include meeting and making alike. Later dictionary examples attest same, unify, together, and assent/follow. Exact dating and semantic links among these senses are not established here; no chronology is inferred from an ordered gloss list.

衕's semantic 行 plus phonetic 同 account is explicit in the received Shuowen wording, but the source also preserves a variant注 reading 周聲. The disagreement is recorded, not resolved. No securely dated early attestation for 衕 was established.

Supplied local Unihan kMandarin rows are 同 tóng and 衕 tòng, but official character-specific pages failed to open; these remain unverified externally. The supplied Baxter–Sagart dataset row for 同 is MC duwng, OC *lˤoŋ; no row for 衕 is available, and no same-system component-host comparison is asserted. Other system reconstructions in the dossier are not merged with Baxter–Sagart.

Commons description establishes the seal-style candidate and reuse terms. Its exact direct SVG URL was linked from the inspected description, but the browser fetch failed with cache miss; no visual inspection is claimed.

The early enclosure's depicted object and its independent name or pronunciation are not established. Thus the specific claim that the whole graph was borrowed for a tube/bucket word remains unverified; reconstructing 同 alone would not establish the object's name.
CUHK reports the seal-script reinterpretation as its paleographic account; this invocation did not inspect artifact images directly. The Commons seal image is a modern redraw.

items.alt: Black seal-script style glyph: an enclosing outline surrounds an inner 口, with a horizontal stroke above it.
items.selection_reason: It illustrates the received seal-script component analysis and the reported reinterpretation of the earlier enclosure. The visible form is a modern redraw, not a dated artifact.
items.rights: Wikimedia Commons file page states that this representation is public domain; attribution is appreciated but not required.

limitations.text: The earlier enclosing shape has competing interpretations: it may depict a tube- or bucket-like object, or may already represent 同. Its identity, name, and pronunciation are unsettled, and this seal-style redraw cannot resolve the disagreement.
